info.title: Junctura Foundation API
info.description: Machine-readable contract for implemented Core routes and planned additions. Planned operations carry x-junctura-status: planned. An x-junctura-planned-operation contains the full future Operation Object at the same path and method as its implemented parent. Mock consumers can replace each parent with its planned operation to build a planned view. The following authority rules apply to implemented routes. Capability Registry, Resolver, Composition, delegation and provider dispatch remain separate design drafts. Reader/writer roles are not OAuth scopes. Tenant/app IDs in caller headers or JSON never supply authority. V2 is backend-only: bind an active registered app to verified tenant/issuer/client_id and operator-enrolled service-account subject. Layer-2 backends enforce human/domain decisions; no on-behalf-of delegation exists. Owner writes and exact expiring read shares are enforced at SQL/storage boundaries. App/owner suspension blocks subsequent v2 access, not already-authorized in-flight work. Workflow and explicitly allowlisted v1 resources remain tenant-scoped. See RESOURCE_AUTHORIZATION.md for migration, logical deletion and retained bytes.

servers.description: Local Compose only; substitute configured PUBLIC_URL. No public deployment is implied.

x-junctura-upstream-boundary: /identity/ is a Keycloak passthrough. Only the documented protocol integration is standardized here; upstream admin/login-action/other protocol surfaces remain governed by the pinned provider, not advertised as Junctura-owned APIs.
x-junctura-routing-errors: For implemented routes: Unsupported methods are normally 405 on health, identity, data, objects, administration and existing workflow instance paths. /ready, workflow definition/execution collections and resource-share routes return 404 for unsupported methods. Authentication, writer checks or resource lookup may reject first. Invalid app/record/object paths can return 400. HEAD always has no wire body. Unknown public routes return 404; Gateway /v1,/v2 auth precedes lookup. Gateway auth errors may be HTML.

put.description: Create or replace the calling app's schema and index configuration. All configured fields are declared top-level properties; uniqueKey, when set, is a required indexed string matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$ on every record. Core validates writes to registered collections and maintains typed field values in shared expression indexes. Existing incompatible records or duplicate values return 409 before activation. An omitted auditActions retains the app-wide catalog; a supplied array replaces it and action names must be unique. The response includes the effective catalog. Unregistered collections retain schemaless writes.

get.description: Count all readable matching records in the selected owner scope. groups is empty for count-only requests. Group keys follow the requested dimension order and missing values group as null. Queries that would return more than 1,000 groups return 400 invalid_query. Management viewers may not filter or group on sensitive fields.

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: Repeat groupBy once per dimension. day(field) buckets an indexed date or date-time by UTC day.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: One condition per indexed top-level field, combined with AND. Operands are JSON scalars (eq), nonempty JSON arrays of scalars (in), ordered JSON numbers/strings (gte/lte) or JSON strings (prefix). Field types must match the schema. Percent-encode query values.

parameters.name: ownerAppId
parameters.description: Defaults to the calling app. Another app's collection yields only records explicitly shared with the caller, including live app-group shares with current membership.

put.summary: Upsert a record by its unique key
put.description: The collection must declare a uniqueKey and data must contain the exact case-sensitive path value. Creating a record returns 201 and may omit If-Match. Replacing an existing record returns 200 and requires If-Match, including while holding its lock. An If-Match for a key with no matching record version returns 412. A lock held by a different caller prevents replacement. Replay the same key, body and precondition to recover the original result.

ETag.description: Strong record version tag for writes by the owner app.
Strong record version tag for writes by the owner app.

post.description: Apply 1–50 creates, replacements, deletions or atomic increment operations in request order in one transaction for the calling app. Every replace and delete requires ifMatch with the current record ETag, even for a schemaless collection or its lock holder. Each increment item applies one or more increments to one record using the atomic PATCH rules and may omit ifMatch. The batch key covers all items. Locks held by other callers block edits and deletes, including increments. Each result matches its input position. Deletes have version null. A failure rolls back the entire batch. Schema violation paths point into the matching operation in the request.

get.summary: Export records owned by the calling app
get.description: Active app owner only. The export covers record IDs and data across its collections. Collection definitions, record revisions, shares, file bytes and audit rows are outside this format.

200.description: Consistent snapshot of records owned by the calling app, ordered by collection and ID. A complete line is LF terminated.

schema.description: UTF-8 JSON lines. Each line follows the schema RecordArchiveLine unless otherwise specified.

post.description: Create the supplied records under the verified calling app in one transaction. Preserve record IDs and create fresh versions. Validate every line, schema, uniqueness and quota. Existing IDs conflict; any failed line rolls back the upload. A line must be a single UTF-8 JSON object. No blank lines.

schema.description: UTF-8 JSON lines. Each line follows the schema RecordArchiveLine unless otherwise specified.

get.summary: List the caller's pending group tasks
get.description: Return each eligible parallel task separately. The verified group path must match the task's unit and one of its candidate groups. All filters narrow that authorized set. overdue is true if dueAt is past at response time. Sort by deadline ascending with undated tasks last, then taskId. claimedBy and claimedUntil describe the active claim and are both null when the task is unclaimed or the claim has expired.

parameters.name: candidateGroup
parameters.description: Optional task group filter. It cannot grant access to a group.

post.description: An eligible member of a candidate group in the task unit may claim the task. The claim expires after 1800 seconds by default and may last up to 28800 seconds. Repeating a claim as the current holder returns the existing expiry without extending it. A claim held by another caller or a completed task returns 409. Core serializes claims and releases with completion. An accepted completion in progress prevents a new claim.
An eligible current holder may release their claim. Repeating release while the waiting task is unclaimed returns 204. An active claim of another caller or an already completed task returns 409.

get.description: Read completed steps newest first by completedAt and taskId. Access requires a verified group eligible on the execution or an enrolled audit.read principal. Core stamps the actor and the matching group used for authorization. If several groups match, use the first in the definition's candidateGroups order. Pending transitions are absent.
An enrolled tenant directory administrator reads rows in ascending identifier order. The existing principal and organization tree are separate views.

put.description: An enrolled directory administrator sets the desired state at the named key. Referenced unit types and parent units must already exist. Success confirms synchronization with the identity provider. Retry the same desired state if synchronization is unavailable. Previously issued tokens can retain old claims until renewed.

delete.description: Deletion conflicts while a unit references the type. Repeating a successful deletion returns 204. Success confirms synchronization with the identity provider. delete.description: Deleting membership removes all of the member's group assignments in this unit. Repeating a successful deletion returns 204. get.summary: Search readable records and clean text files
get.description: Search registered searchable record fields and text extracted from clean files. Core applies live tenant, ownership and exact read-share checks before returning results. Sensitive field matches are excluded for management viewers. Results contain references only. Order by relevance with a stable resource ID tie-breaker. Index updates are asynchronous.

Connect with the Authorization bearer header. Receive new workflow tasks for eligible groups, record status changes for readable records and consent revocations for the subject or affected app. Each SSE event has a named event field and one JSON data line containing references only. The connection is live-only and has no event IDs or replay. Reconnect and refresh source lists after disconnect. Core closes the stream when authentication expires and rechecks authorization before delivery.

200.description: UTF-8 server-sent event stream. Comment-only heartbeat frames carry no data.
GET metadata with an empty body.

get.description: Dependency check, not transaction success or full DR. Other methods return 404.

get.description: Without sort, use the existing (created_at, id) order. Supply nextCursor with unchanged owner, filters and ordering. Data returned to authorized management readers omits sensitive fields. Filtering and sorting on those fields are unavailable to these readers. Shared reads include only live exact shares and live app-group shares with current membership. Missing or inaccessible owner scope returns 404. In compatibility mode, a list without the new filter parameters may retain the legacy body and cursor without version fields.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: One condition per indexed top-level field, combined with AND. Operands are JSON scalars (eq), nonempty JSON arrays of scalars (in), ordered JSON numbers/strings (gte/lte) or JSON strings (prefix). Field types must match the schema. Percent-encode query values.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort by a declared indexed field. Missing and null values sort last, and id breaks ties in the requested direction. Mutually exclusive with order.

parameters.name: ownerAppId

post.description: Only the owner app writes. Validate data against the registered schema, if any, and enforce the unique field and collection quota. Compact UTF-8 JSON in data is limited to 64 KiB across write endpoints. New records start at version 1. An Idempotency-Key enables the versioned response. A server in compatibility mode also accepts requests without the key and returns the legacy body with an ETag. Strict mode requires the key.

ETag.description: Strong record version tag for writes by the owner app.

get.description: Returns the current representation. An owner receives the strong ETag to use on a subsequent write. Existing records start at version 1. An authorized management reader sees data with sensitive top-level fields omitted. Masking grants no read permission. Strict mode includes version in the response body. Compatibility mode retains the legacy body. Shared and management reads omit the write ETag.

ETag.description: Strong record version tag for writes by the owner app.

patch.summary: Replace record data or increment numeric fields
patch.description: The data form replaces the complete data object and checks schema and uniqueness. The operations form is the only edit that may omit If-Match, because it updates server-side without a client read. An If-Match supplied with operations must still match. An Idempotency-Key is required for operations. A lock held by a different caller blocks either form. An increment uses the current value of a declared top-level numeric indexed field. by, min and max are numbers. Bounds are optional and inclusive, and min must be at most max. A nonnumeric or absent value, an ineligible field or inverted bounds returns 400. Process increments in array order and apply them together in one database statement. A bound failure returns 409 limit_exceeded with the field name. A successful write increments the record version once and validates the resulting data against the collection schema. Strict mode requires If-Match for replacements. Compatibility mode accepts its omission and preserves the legacy replacement body. An atomic increment always returns a versioned body.

ETag.description: Strong record version tag for writes by the owner app.

delete.description: In strict mode the owner must supply If-Match for every existing record, including in schemaless collections and while holding the record lock. A missing required tag or stale tag leaves the record unchanged. A lock held by a different caller prevents deletion. Compatibility mode accepts an omitted If-Match.

post.summary: Acquire or renew a record lock
post.description: The owner app may acquire an exclusive lock for 300 seconds by default, up to 1800 seconds per request. Core binds the lock to the verified app and, when present, its verified delegated user. To renew an active lock, send its lockId in the body and a fresh Idempotency-Key. Renewal sets the expiry relative to the renewal time and retains the lockId. Acquiring without lockId while already holding the active lock returns that lock without extending it. A stale lockId returns 409 resource_conflict. A lock held by another caller returns 423. Core checks the active lock in the same transaction as each record mutation. Locks expire automatically and leave the record ETag unchanged.

delete.description: Only the holder of the active lock may release it, using the exact Lock-Id. Administrators cannot force release. If the record exists and has no active lock, return 204. An active lock held by another caller returns 423. An active lock held by this caller with a different lockId returns 409 resource_conflict.

post.description: Active registered backend resolved from verified tenant/issuer/client_id and exact operator-enrolled resource_subject. Owner-only mutations; individually shared reads. Suspension/revocation and disabled enrollment block access. Upload 1 byte to 5 MiB. Stable-UUID PUT with identical bytes is retryable; POST creates a new ID and is not blindly retried. V2 DELETE tombstones permanently; bytes/old versions retained. PUT publishes immutable versions after DB reauthorization; concurrent owner PUTs use last publication. UUIDs are tenant-scoped, so a foreign tenant may create independent bytes at the same UUID.

x-junctura-planned-operation.summary: Upload an object with optional metadata
x-junctura-planned-operation.description: The file part must be 1 byte–5 MiB and is published only after a clean scan. A recordRef may point to a live record owned by the caller. The link and tags confer no read access. Charge the bytes of current published objects to the per-app quota before publication. Replacement charges the size delta; deletion releases the current size. The octet-stream form creates an unlinked and untagged object. For multipart uploads the logical request includes file bytes, link and tags. Multipart boundaries are transport framing and do not change the logical request.

get.summary: List authorized objects by record or tag
get.description: Return current clean object metadata readable with existing ownership or exact share grants. Match both filters when supplied. Use recordRef[collection] and recordRef[id] together. Sort by object ID. Record links alone never grant visibility.

post.summary: Share a resource with an app or a record with an app group
post.description: Use granteeAppId for an exact app recipient or granteeAppGroup for one same-tenant operator-managed app label. A group share applies to one record and expires within 24 hours, like an exact app share. Active membership is checked at read time; expiry, revocation or app suspension terminates subsequent reads. Existing revoke-by-shareId also revokes group shares. Shares grant no write or onward grant authority. A supplied Idempotency-Key replays the original share instead of creating another.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Supply a stable UUID for replay safety. Existing exact-app shares remain accepted without it in compatibility mode.

delete.description: Owning backend only. Repeat revocation returns 204; hidden IDs return 404. Unsupported methods return 404. Audit and revocation are atomic.

post.description: Live operator-enrolled human principal, exact issuer/subject/management-client/tenant binding. Baseline core-reader suffices; core-writer is not administrative authority. Core errors include requestId; Gateway auth errors may be HTML or JSON without requestId. Exact owner/client/origin enrollment required; duplicate client binding conflicts even after revocation. No POST retry guarantee.

get.description: Requires a normal bearer token with verified client_id and an enabled audit.read principal. All aggregates are scoped to the caller tenant and issuer. Returns counts and timestamps, application IDs, display names and states only; record content, collection names, object keys, file names, capability manifests, grant proposals, subjects and audit reasons are never returned. File aggregates use /junctura-app/<tenant>/<applicationId>; files is null when objects storage is unconfigured. Responses use Cache-Control: no-store.

200.description: Tenant- and issuer-scoped counts and timestamps; only application display names are disclosed.

400.description: invalid_query: any query string, including an empty query delimiter, is rejected.

403.description: stats_permission_required: caller must be an enabled audit.read principal in its own tenant, issuer, subject and management client. verified_client_required: verified client_id is missing. Standard bearer authorization failures also apply.

503.description: application_stats_unavailable: data storage is unconfigured, a dependency is unavailable or an aggregate is malformed. Identity dependency failures also fail closed.

x-junctura-planned-operation.description: unit is the business execution's default task unit and defaults to the deployment binding. taskUnits overrides it for selected BPMN userTask element IDs. The caller must be authorized by the deployed workflow policy for all named units. A business execution needs a resolved unit for every task. dueAt is the optional execution deadline and default for its steps. taskDueAt overrides it for the listed BPMN userTask element IDs each time they activate. Unknown element IDs are invalid. Deadlines mark work overdue without preventing completion. The start key binds definition, input, unit assignments and deadlines. An identical retry replays the original 201 result.

x-junctura-planned-operation.description: Read the execution in the verified tenant. dueAt is null when no execution deadline was supplied. Use the task inbox for individually authorized pending steps.

delete.description: Workflow resources remain TENANT scoped, not app-private. App suspension is not a workflow permission check. Keep private payloads out of tenant-visible variables. Repeated cancellation returns 204; completed execution returns 409. No rollback of external effects is implied.

x-junctura-planned-operation.description: Cancel a running execution in the caller tenant. Repeated cancellation returns 204. A completed execution or an accepted task completion still pending reconciliation returns 409. Cancellation and completion are serialized for the execution.

post.description: Workflow resources remain TENANT scoped, not app-private. App suspension is not a workflow permission check. Keep private payloads out of tenant-visible variables. Empty object only. Completes exactly one active user task. Already completed is replayed; cancelled or multiple active tasks conflict. No task-assignee/business approval policy is inferred.

x-junctura-planned-operation.description: Business workflows require taskId. Core checks execution, tenant, unit and candidate-group membership before accepting the command, including replays. A task claimed by another caller returns 409 task_claimed; a completed task returns 409 task_already_completed for a new attempt. A valid claim by the caller or an unclaimed task can be completed. variables supplies primitive BPMN routing values and replaces the proposed output field. Optional records are creates owned by the calling app; using them requires an active binding for that app and a verified user context. Core validates and commits them with a durable completion outbox entry. A 202 means the task transition is still pending. An identical replay with the original Idempotency-Key returns the first result even if the task has since completed. Read execution state and history after a 202. Other parallel tasks remain pending. While an accepted completion is pending, cancellation conflicts. The empty object is reserved for the legacy technical checkpoint and returns the execution representation.

200.description: Selected task completed or an identical completion was replayed.

202.description: Records and outbox committed; task transition pending.

PlannedIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
PlannedIdempotencyKey.description: Required UUID for this write. A missing or malformed key returns 400 invalid_request. Core retains the first recorded result for 24 hours, scoped to the verified tenant and caller, HTTP method and concrete request path. Within that window, the same key and logical request replay the first status, body and resource headers without another write. A changed body or write precondition for the same key returns 422 idempotency_key_reused. Concurrent identical requests share one result; every replay requires current authorization.

RecordOptionalIdempotencyKey.description: With a key, an identical request replays its original response within 24 hours.

RecordCreateIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

RecordIfMatch.name: If-Match
RecordIfMatch.description: Send the exact strong ETag from the record response. Required for every delete or replacement of an existing record, including in schemaless collections and when the caller holds the record lock. Missing returns 428; stale returns 412.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size for record lists. Unknown or repeated list query keys return 400 invalid_query. Item GET validates the first limit value but returns at most one row; repeated limit uses its first value.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Tenant-scoped workflow key; identical definition/input returns existing execution, changed logical input conflicts.

RecordOrder.name: order
RecordOrder.description: Order by created_at and then id in this direction. Use the same order on every page. Invalid values return 400 invalid_query.

RecordCursor.name: cursor
RecordCursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Malformed cursors or a cursor order different from the requested order return 400 invalid_cursor.

AtomicIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
AtomicIdempotencyKey.description: Required when the PATCH body contains operations. The planned Idempotency-Key replay and 24-hour retention rules apply when a key is supplied.

ConditionalRecordIfMatch.name: If-Match
ConditionalRecordIfMatch.description: Send the exact strong ETag from the record response. Required when the request replaces existing data. Atomic increments and creation by unique key may omit it. If supplied, a missing or stale record version returns 412.

RecordLockId.name: Lock-Id
RecordLockId.description: The lockId from the active lock response.
